en: visit someone who cannot go out (in hospital, prison, or army)

examples.ko: 입대한 친구를 면회하러 새벽부터 기차를 탔어요.
examples.en: I took a train from dawn to visit my friend who joined the army.

examples.ko: 병원에서는 환자를 면회하는 시간이 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital has set times for visiting patients.

examples.ko: 삼십 분만 면회해도 되는지 간호사에게 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I asked the nurse if I could visit for just thirty minutes.

examples.ko: 이 병원에서 환자를 면회하려면 먼저 예약해야 해요.
examples.en: To visit a patient at this hospital, you have to book first.

examples.ko: 어제 동생을 면회하고 맛있는 걸 사 줬어요.
examples.en: Yesterday I visited my younger sibling and bought them something tasty.

examples.ko: 감염 예방 때문에 지금은 직접 면회할 수 없어요.
examples.en: To prevent infection, you can't visit in person right now.

explain: '만나다'와 달리 군대, 병원, 교도소처럼 마음대로 나올 수 없는 곳에 있는 사람을 찾아가 만날 때 써요. 보통 '면회(를) 가다/오다'라고 하고, '면회 시간'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Unlike '만나다' (to meet), it is for going to see someone who cannot freely leave a place, such as the military, a hospital or a prison. People usually say '면회(를) 가다/오다', and the noun is common too, as in '면회 시간' (visiting hours).

examples.en: The masseur carefully loosened my shoulders.
I got a back massage from a masseur.
I am studying to get a massage therapist license.
This masseur has really strong hands.
There is a well-known masseur in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 안마사께 조금 더 세게 해 달라고 부탁했어요.
examples.en: I asked the masseur to press a little harder.

explain: 안마를 직업으로 하는 사람을 말해요. 일상에서는 '마사지'라는 말도 많이 써서, 마사지를 해 주는 사람을 '마사지사'라고도 해요. 누군가의 몸을 직접 주물러 주는 사람이라서 '안마기'와는 달리 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who works as a masseur. In daily life people also use the word '마사지', so someone who gives massages may be called a '마사지사'. Unlike '안마기', which is a machine, this word refers to a person.

examples.ko: 올해 우리 회사에 연수생 열 명이 들어왔어요.
examples.en: Ten trainees joined our company this year.

examples.ko: 저는 해외 연수생으로 일 년 동안 일본에 있었어요.
examples.en: I was in Japan for a year as an overseas trainee.
The trainees receive training every morning.
I'm still a trainee, so there's a lot I don't know yet.
I explained the company rules to the trainee.

examples.ko: 한국어 연수생을 위한 수업이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: There are separate classes for Korean-language trainees.

explain: 회사나 기관에서 일을 배우거나, 어학연수처럼 일정 기간 교육을 받는 사람이에요. '연수'가 교육을 받는 일을 뜻해서 '연수를 받다'와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It means someone who learns the work at a company or institution, or takes a training program for a set period such as language study abroad. Since '연수' means training, it often appears with '연수를 받다'.

examples.en: The company invited overseas buyers to the event.
The university invites a famous writer.
We will invite only family to the wedding.
I sent an invitation letter to the guests.

examples.ko: 외국에서 온 손님을 공식 만찬에 초청하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to invite a guest from abroad to the official dinner.

examples.ko: 선생님이 우리를 저녁 식사에 초청해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Our teacher invited us to dinner.

explain: 행사나 모임에 정식으로 부를 때 써요. 친구를 집에 부르는 가벼운 상황에서는 '초대하다'를 써요. 명사는 '초청장', '초청 강연'처럼 붙여요.
explain_en: It is used for formally inviting someone to an event or gathering. For a light situation, such as asking a friend to your home, use '초대하다'. The noun attaches in words like '초청장' (invitation card) and '초청 강연' (invited lecture).

examples.en: There is an alumni get-together this weekend.
The company is collecting dues for the social club.
I met my seniors after a long time at the get-together.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 친목회는 한 달에 한 번 모여요.
examples.en: Our neighborhood social club meets once a month.
I'm busy these days because I took on the role of treasurer of the social club.

examples.ko: 그 모임은 이름은 친목회지만 실제로는 사업 이야기만 해요.
examples.en: That group is called a social club, but they only talk business.

explain: 서로 친해지려고 모이는 모임이에요. 같은 취미로 모이는 '동호회', 같은 학교 출신이 모이는 '동창회'와 달리 특별한 조건 없이 가볍게 모여요. '친목회를 하다/열다/가다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a group that meets just to get closer to each other. Unlike a '동호회' (hobby club) or '동창회' (alumni association), it often has no special condition. You say '친목회를 하다/열다/가다'.
